title: No Wrapped Ether
brief: Compliance says the treasury must never hold WETH. The Safe runs on a permissive catch-all, so the team denied wrapping on WETH. The auditors still found WETH in the Safe. Stop all wrapping, and keep paying Dave in ETH and Erin in USDC.

rules.note: Allows every CALL without its own rule

tests.label: Pay Erin 500 USDC again next week
Send 1 ETH to WETH with nothing attached
Send 1 ETH to WETH with a made-up action
Send 1 ETH to WETH with another made-up action

hints: WETH wraps any ETH it receives, whatever is attached. Most of those calls never reach the Wrap ETH rule.
You cannot block every action WETH does not have. Ask instead what the Safe should be allowed to do.
Drop the catch-all. Give plain ETH to Dave and USDC to Erin rules of their own.
explain: WETH wraps ETH sent with nothing attached, and with any action it does not know. Those calls miss the deny rule and land on the catch-all. A blocklist cannot win against that: denying each made-up action here passes these tests and misses the next one. An allowlist can: with no permissive catch-all, every call to WETH is denied by default. Always Allow on the two new rules works too; Plain ETH Transfer and the Recipient Allowlist also keep them to plain ETH and to Erin.
